Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice M G Uma
 Oral Order
Petitioners being accused Nos.2 and 3 are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated
against them by respondent No.2 in Cr.No.109/2019 of Mudigere police station now pending in Sc
No.10/2020 on the file of the learned Ii Additional District and Sessions Judge, Chikkamangaluru,
registered for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 313, 323, 504, 506 R/w Section 34 of
Indian Penal Code (for short 'the Ipc') and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

2. Heard Sri.Jagadish Baliga N., learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. Kethan Kumar, learned counsel for NC: 2025:KHC:706 respondent No.1 and Smt. Rashmi Patel, learned HCGP for respondent No.2.
3.

In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the Petitioners have made out any grounds to allow the petition and to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners has produced the copy of order dated 20.12.2023 passed in Mics.
First Appeal No.7710/2022 before this Court
wherein, the divorce petition filed by respondent No.2 and accused No.1 was allowed.
Divorce was granted as they were residing separately since more than 3 years.
There is no chance of reunion.
The order also makes it clear that the parties have entered into settlement as stated in their application.
They mutually agreed for divorce.
They withdrew allegations made against one NC: 2025:KHC:706 another and respondent No.2 herein had agreed to give up her claim for alimony.

Paragraph 8 of the order refers SC No.10/2020 i.e.,
criminal proceedings in question in this petition and that respondent No.2 has agreed to co-operate with accused No.1 for quashing the said criminal proceedings.
5.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 agreed to the terms of settlement and also granting of divorce.
He submitted that parties are residing separately and that he has no objection to allow the petition.
6. Petitioners being accused Nos.2 and 3, sister-in-law and mother-in-law of respondent No.2 are entitled for the benefit of settlement entered into between respondent Nos.2 and accused No.1.

In view of the above, I am of the opinion that the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners is liable to be quashed.
7.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is allowed.

NC: 2025:KHC:706 (ii) The FIR registered against the petitioners in Cr.No.109/2019 of Mudigere police station now pending in SC No.10/2020 on the file of the learned II Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Chikkamangaluru, registered the offence punishable under Section 498A, 313, 323, 504, 506 R/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, is hereby quashed.
